summary.name: Google's Site Reliability Engineering with Todd Underwood
summary.one_liner: A Software Engineering Daily podcast episode in which Google director of site reliability engineering Todd Underwood discusses the SRE role, its relation to devops, and Google's Borg cluster system.
use_cases: Learning how Google's SRE role works
Understanding how SRE relates to devops
Background on Google's Borg data center system
Listening to an interview about running highly available services
Context for reading the O'Reilly SRE book
summary.what_it_does: This page is a podcast episode page for Software Engineering Daily, featuring an interview with Todd Underwood, a director of site reliability engineering at Google. It covers how the SRE role relates to devops and the relationship between engineers developing Google services and the SREs who maintain them. The episode also discusses Borg, Google's internal data center operating system. The page references O'Reilly's book "Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems" as a source on the role. The text is a short description and does not include a transcript.
notable: Interview with a Google director of site reliability engineering
Discusses Google's internal Borg data center operating system
Covers the relationship between SRE and devops
Points to the O'Reilly SRE book on Google production systems
caveats: Page text is a brief episode description only; no transcript or full details are included
Borg is an internal Google system and is discussed only at a high level
